content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've been trying to set up a Modbus connection between [product_name] and an EasyIO FG32+ over the past several days, but without success. Although most of you may not have experience with EasyIO controllers, I'm hoping someone can assist with configuring [product_name]. Both devices appear to connect and recognize each other, but I'm unable to read or write data. I've attempted using network input/output directly as well as reading to and from the VM on the diagram. Pictures and EasyIO PDF manuals are included in a zip file. Thank you.
Here’s the EasyIO Modbus Master documentation.
This is the EasyIO slave documentation.

Hello [user_name], and welcome to the forum. I noticed your zip file contains only screenshots, not the EasyIO manuals. While I’m not familiar with EasyIO controllers, I suggest making the EasyIO device the server instead of [product_name]. Edit: I see now that you uploaded the manuals separately. You could have included all files in one zip archive as well.

Sorry, the file was too large so I added the manuals in the following posts. I've tried both configurations, client and server, but haven't achieved results. My question is whether I've mapped and set the parameters correctly. I think the next step is to contact EasyIO support. Thanks for your reply. Edit: This is my first Modbus project, so I'm probably making mistakes.
I’m unable to give a definitive answer. The provided manuals are not very detailed and focus mainly on setting up the EasyIO device.

The EasyIO FG32+ seems like an interesting product, but your instructions are limited. I’m aware that drivers for Modbus TCP should be installed on the device, but your screenshots don’t make this clear. I’ve attached a [product_name] server for testing and some additional files showing Modbus addresses for different operands. Maybe these will assist you. Regards, [user_name]

Hello, Sorry for the delayed response—work has kept me busy this week. [user_name], all necessary software appears installed and functioning (see attachment); previously, I wasn't even sure if EasyIO recognized the connected client. When I create more links from [product_name] to EasyIO, they're displayed immediately. Disconnecting [product_name] makes the connected devices count go to zero in EasyIO, then back again when reconnecting. So, they communicate but data still isn’t being transmitted. From what I see, configuring [product_name] only requires setting up the network input, and it should work. I think the best approach now is to reach out to EasyIO support, since they likely have experience with [product_name]. EasyIO controllers are great for simple automation tasks like HVAC or lighting control, but they're less suited for high-speed processes. Take a look at [url] for more details. Thanks to both of you for your help. Regards.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing problems establishing Modbus communication between [product_name] and an EasyIO FG32+, with devices connecting but not exchanging data successfully. Both client and server configurations were attempted, but the core issue with data transfer remains. Limited documentation for EasyIO adds to the difficulty of troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates a simple and effective setup for Modbus TCP data exchange between [product_name] and EasyIO FG32+. Improved documentation and more intuitive configuration process for [product_name] would enhance their experience.
